title: Proactive tenant fractional reservation & burst-smoothing proof-of-concept
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During the Feb 10th capacity incident several tenants experienced long tail latencies and intermittent evictions despite what our reservation signals suggested. Postmortem identified three contributing issues: (1) coarse-grained reservation sizing that assigns whole-GPU quotas causing fragmentation; (2) burst tokenbucket parameters that permit sustained bursts under load and then aggressively evict; (3) limited telemetry for quickly detecting noisy-tenant KV-cache leaks and multi-tenant interference.

Goal: Deliver a proof-of-concept (PoC) that demonstrates: fractional/reservations-at-subGPU granularity, an adaptive burst-smoothing algorithm that decays burst tokens proportional to observed QPS/seq-length, and improved telemetry & mitigation hooks to auto-quarantine noisy tenants before cluster-wide degradation. The PoC should be safe to run in a canary Dedicated cluster and produce measurable improvement in 95/99th tail latency and eviction rate under synthetic multi-tenant blast tests.

Scope: This ticket covers design, prototype implementation, canary rollout plan, dashboards, and preliminary evaluation. Follow-up tickets will (a) harden and generalize algorithms, (b) integrate into autoscaler and billing, (c) update runbooks and SLA docs.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change billing semantics, does not modify user-facing config APIs, and will not ship telemetry retention changes longer than 30 days.
acceptance_criteria: 1) PoC implements fractional reservation allocator (sub-GPU slots) with per-tenant adjustable weight. 2) Burst-smoothing algorithm deployed behind a feature flag; can be toggled per-cluster. 3) New telemetry: per-tenant tail-latency histograms, eviction-probability, kv-cache-miss-rate exported to Datadog. 4) Canary run (72h) shows >=30% reduction in 99th latency for noisy mixes and <5% false-positive tenant quarantines. 5) PRs merged and Confluence design doc published. 6) Runbook updated with quarantine rollback steps.
steps: Design fractional reservation format and in-memory allocator API (runtime + orchestrator)
Implement burst-smoothing: token decay window based on moving-average QPS and sequence-length distribution
Add telemetry hooks for per-tenant histograms and eviction-probability signal
Create canary cluster config and feature flags; prepare synthetic multi-tenant workload generator
Run bench tests and iterate on thresholds to avoid false-positive quarantines
Prepare dashboards and alert rules; coordinate with SRE for canary monitoring
Ship PoC, collect 72h results, and document outcomes and follow-ups
comments: 2026-02-20 | Aisha Patel: Created ticket after Feb 10 postmortem. Initial design sketched; linked incident notes and test harness. Assigned to Riley for prototype work.

2026-02-25 | Riley Torres: Completed allocator design doc and added API sketch. Decided to implement fractional reservations as weight fractions (0.01-1.0) mapped to soft cgroups + scheduler tokens to avoid changing billing. Opening PR for allocator core loop next week.

2026-02-28 | Marcus Chen (SRE): Canary cluster prepared (dedicated-canary-03). Agreed to run canary behind feature flag and pre-authorized rollbacks; created temporary alert policy for eviction spikes.

2026-03-02 | Riley Torres: Implemented burst-smoothing prototype. Chose exponential decay with adaptive window size driven by 1-minute and 5-minute moving averages. Early local sims show 20-35% reduction in sustained eviction events for synthetic noisy tenants.

2026-03-04 | Priya Nair (PM): Coordinated PRD update and customer communication template in case canary affects production. Confirmed customers with Dedicated instances will not be auto-billed for PoC changes.

2026-03-05 | Riley Torres: Instrumentation added for per-tenant 95/99 histograms and eviction-probability metric. Preparing bench run 03-07 to validate thresholds and measure false-positive quarantines.
next_steps: 1) Run synthetic blend (40 tenants with 3 noisy tenants) on canary 72h starting 2026-03-07. 2) Tune token decay constants to target <5% FP quarantines. 3) If metrics meet acceptance, schedule Extension ticket to move to staging and add billing hooks.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly aggressive quarantine could evict healthy tenants. Mitigation: Start with conservative thresholds, require two independent signals (eviction-probability + kv-cache-miss-rate spike) to trigger quarantine. Risk: Fractional reservations could complicate scheduler fairness math. Mitigation: Add unit tests and deterministic simulation harness; gate behind feature flag and canary cluster.
owner_notes: Keep customer impact communication short and proactive. If quarantine triggers, SRE must notify product and operations immediately and start rollback within 10 minutes. Document any tuning decisions and rationale in Confluence for auditability.
